correctness.rationale: The backward generator is Δ_x+γ∂²_θ+p e_θ·∇_x. The passive killed heat resolvent R has bounded e_θ·∇_x R on bounded functions (integrable t^(-1/2) Dirichlet heat-gradient bound at short times and exponential decay at long times, also with static θ); R(I−p e_θ·∇_x R)^(-1) gives a convergent expansion near zero. Angle translation by π eliminates odd averaged powers. At first order the first harmonic is f(r)cos(θ−arg x), with f=−A_γ^(-1)r/2. The averaged second-order forcing is −(rf)'/(2r); regularity at the center and absorption give G(r)=∫_r^1 f(s)ds/2. Integration gives the stated Bessel expression and f_0=(r³−r)/16 gives the zero-rotation endpoint. Writing f=rh reduces positivity of A_γ^(-1) to the radial four-dimensional Dirichlet resolvent, proving strict sign and ∂_γf=A_γ^(-2)r/2>0 inside. With k=√γ, k³G(1−z/k)=[I_0(k)/I_1(k)−I_0(k−z)/I_1(k)−z+z²/(2k)]/4. The standard large-argument expansion is uniform for bounded z and gives the claimed layer, including z=0 by the zero Dirichlet extension. At fixed r<1 the second Bessel ratio is exponentially small (also at r=0) and the first is 1+O(1/k), giving the bulk remainder. No joint p–γ estimate was used.
residual_risks: The remainder is local in propulsion for fixed γ; the layer concerns G alone.

The 2025 first harmonic also yields G by the averaged quadratic radial Poisson equation and a single quadrature; the paper's passage stops at the order of the correction.

value.rationale: The fixed-start quadratic escape-time response is the first nonvanishing weak-activity effect for uniform orientation. Its sign, order with rotation, and near-wall scaling quantify meaningful transport behavior not apparent from the unaveraged first harmonic or a fixed-radius expansion. This value assessment does not certify distinctness.
